title: Continuous Integration's Roots in Extreme Programming (late 1990s–2000)
explainer: "Continuous integration" was named as one of the original practices of Extreme Programming, the discipline Kent Beck articulated in the late 1990s. Martin Fowler then documented the practice in a widely read essay describing a real ThoughtWorks project around 2000, where merging and testing work constantly — instead of in rare, big-bang integrations — cut down on painful last-minute breakage. CI tools today automate exactly that XP practice, which is why "integrate early and often" still sits at the center of what CI is for.
